raw_text:
MIAX Sapphire — Listing Alert — MIAX Exchange Group - Options Markets - Qualified Securities for Q4 2026
Listing Alert MIAX Sapphire October 01, 2026 | 05:57 PM MIAX Exchange Group - Options Markets - Qualified Securities for Q4 2026 As previously announced in the January 20, 2026 Alert and August 17, 2026 Alert, the MIAX Options Exchanges filed with the SEC to amend the Short Term Option Series Program of each exchange. The Short Term Option Series Program was amended to include, in addition to the up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations for options on certain individual stocks: (1) adding up to two Tuesday and Thursday expirations for options on Exchange-Traded Fund ("ETF") Shares that meet a higher threshold of criteria "Qualifying Securities" criteria, and (2) adding up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations for options on ETF Shares that meet a lower-threshold set of criteria. A Qualifying Security is (1) an underlying security, as measured on the last day of the prior calendar quarter, must have: (A) a market capitalization of greater than 700 billion dollars for an individual stock based on the closing price, or (B) (i) Assets under Management (“AUM”) greater than 50 billion dollars for an Exchange-Traded Fund Share based on net asset value (“NAV”); or (ii) AUM greater than 25 billion dollars for an Exchange-Traded Fund Share based on NAV; (2) monthly options volume, as measured by sides traded in the last month preceding the quarter end, of greater than 10 million options; or monthly options volume, as measured by sides traded in the last month preceding the quarter end, of greater than 5 million options for an Exchange-Traded Fund Share that qualified for (B)(ii) above; (3) a position limit of at least 250,000 contracts; and (4) participate in the Penny Interval Program. ETFs meeting the criteria of an AUM greater than $50 billion, monthly options volume greater than 10 million contracts, a position limit of at least 250,000 contracts, and participation in the Penny Interval Program, are "Tier 1 Qualifying Securities" and are eligible for up to two Monday/Tuesday/ Wednesday/ Thursday expirations. ETFs meeting the criteria of an AUM greater than $25 billion, monthly options volume greater than 5 million contracts, a position limit of at least 250,000 contracts, and participation in the Penny Interval Program, are "Tier 2 Qualifying Securities" and are eligible for up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations. The new series will follow the existing Short Term Option Series Program process of same strike-price intervals, P.M.-settled, and skips any week where the expiration would coincide with a standard, monthly, or quarterly expiration. A Qualifying Security expiration would not be listed on a day when there will be an earnings announcement that takes place after market close. The following securities are Qualified Securities for Q4 2026: Individual Stock Qualifying Securities: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) Alphabet, Inc. (GOOGL) Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) Apple Inc. (AAPL) Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) Micron Technology, Inc. (MU) Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) ETF Tier 1 Qualifying Securities: Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF) iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) ETF Tier 2 Qualifying Securities: iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF (IEF) iShares iBoxx $ Invst Grade Corporate Bond ETF (LQD) iShares Silver Trust (SLV) iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF (GDX) ProShares UltraPro QQQ (TQQQ) Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE) VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) Each calendar quarter, the above criteria will be reassessed to determine eligibility for the following quarter as a Qualifying Security. Investment Company Cross Trading

The Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission") is proposing to amend the rule under the Investment Company Act of 1940 (the "Investment Company Act") that permits securities transactions between a registered investment company and certain affiliates (referred to as "cross trades"), subject to conditions. The proposed amendments are designed to expand the scope of securities that are eligible for cross trading, modernize the rule's conditions, and enhance investor protection. The Commission also proposes to require aggregated reporting of trading activity and cross trades in Form N- PORT and Form N-MFP.

raw_text:
Adviser and Regulated Fund Custody Rules; Crypto Custody Rules

The Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission" or the "SEC") is proposing new custody rules under the Investment Company Act of 1940 (the "Investment Company Act") and amendments to related reporting and recordkeeping requirements to address how regulated investment companies may custody crypto securities and similar investments, and amendments to the custody rule and related reporting and recordkeeping rules under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act") to address how registered investment advisers may custody client crypto funds and securities. We are also proposing to amend the current custody rules to modernize their requirements, to better address current industry practices and feedback, and to implement certain conforming amendments. We are also proposing amendments to the recordkeeping rules under the Investment Company Act and Advisers Act related to these proposed modernization amendments to the custody rules. Additionally, we are proposing to redesignate the custody rule under the Advisers Act and to make corresponding amendments to Form ADV and Form ADV-E for registered investment advisers to reflect the Advisers Act custody rule redesignation. We are also proposing amendments to Form ADV for registered investment advisers and Form N-CEN for regulated investment companies and to improve the quality of public disclosures made on these forms. We are also proposing to add new questions to Form ADV and Form N-CEN related to tokenized private funds and regulated investment company shares, respectively.

title: D33. How should the tradingSession field be populated for option orders?
raw_text:
D33. How should the tradingSession field be populated for option orders?

The tradingSession must be populated with the trading session(s) during which an order is eligible to trade.

For certain options that are eligible to trade on the Cboe Exchange, Inc. during extended global market hours sessions (generally from 8:15 pm T-1 to 9:15 am Eastern Time) and/or regular market hours sessions, the tradingSession field must be populated with:

-    'REG' (Regular Only), for orders only eligible to trade during regular market hours; or 
-    'ALL' (All Sessions), for orders eligible to trade during extended global market hours, regular market hours, and the Curb session.
-    'REGPOST' (Regular and Post Market), for orders eligible to trade during regular market hours and the Curb session.

I. Introduction On February 10, 2026, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. (``FINRA'') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (``SEC'' or ``Commission''), pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (``Exchange Act'') and Rule 19b-4 thereunder, a proposed rule change to amend FINRA Rule 2210 (Communications with the Public) to allow a member broker-dealer (``member'') to project performance or provide a targeted return with respect to a security, a securities portfolio, or an asset allocation or other investment strategy in its communications with the public, subject to specified conditions. The proposed rule change was published for public comment in the Federal Register on February 25, 2026. The comment period closed on March 18, 2026. The Commission received comment letters in response to the Notice. On April 7, 2026, FINRA consented to extend until May 26, 2026, the time period in which the Commission must approve the proposed rule change, disapprove the proposed rule change, or institute proceedings to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change. On May 18, 2026, the Commission received a letter from FINRA stating, among other things, that it anticipated submitting a response to comments, as well as amendments to the proposed rule change. On May 20, 2026, the Commission published an order instituting proceedings to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change (``OIP''). The Commission received comment letters in response to the OIP. On June 30, 2026, FINRA responded to the comment letters received in response to the Notice and OIP and filed a partial amendment to the proposed rule change (``Partial Amendment No. 1''). The proposed rule change, as modified by Partial Amendment No. 1 (hereinafter referred to as the ``proposed rule change'' unless otherwise stated), was published for public comment in the Federal Register on July 7, 2026. On July 21, 2026, FINRA consented to extend until October 23, 2026, the time period in which the Commission must approve or disapprove the proposed rule change. The Commission received comment letters in response to Notice II. On October 14, 2026, FINRA responded to the comment letters received in response to Notice II. This order approves the proposed rule change. II. Description of the Proposed Rule Change FINRA Rule 2210 generally prohibits communications with the public that predict or project performance. As discussed below, there are three exceptions to this general prohibition; the proposed rule change would create a fourth exception in limited circumstances. A. FINRA Rule 2210 (Communications With the Public) Among other things, FINRA Rule 2210 imposes restrictions on the content of a member's communications with the public. For example, FINRA Rule 2210(d)(1) (General Standards) (hereinafter the ``general content standards'') requires, among other things, that: (1) all member communications be based on principles of fair dealing and good faith, be fair and balanced, and provide a sound basis for evaluating the facts in regard to any particular security or type of security, industry, or service; and (2) the member: (a) not omit any material fact or qualification if the omission, in light of the context of the material presented, would cause the communication to be misleading; (b) not make any false, exaggerated, unwarranted, promissory, or misleading statement or claim in the communication; and (c) consider the nature of the audience to which the communication will be directed and provide details and explanations appropriate to the audience. The general content standards also prohibit a communication prepared by a member from predicting or projecting performance, implying that past performance will recur, or making any exaggerated or unwarranted claim, opinion, or forecast. This general prohibition, however, does not apply to communications that contain: (1) certain hypothetical illustrations of mathematical principles; (2) certain investment analysis tools or written reports produced by such investment analysis tools; and (3) certain price targets contained in research reports on debt or equity securities. B. The Proposed Rule Change The proposed rule change would adopt a fourth exception to FINRA Rule 2210(d)(1)(F) to permit members' communications to project performance or provide targeted returns with respect to a security, a securities portfolio, or an asset allocation or other investment strategy (hereinafter, ``projected performance or targeted returns''), subject to the conditions described, in turn, below. 1. Written Policies and Procedures The proposed rule change would require any member that communicates projected performance or targeted returns to adopt and implement written policies and procedures reasonably designed to ensure that the communication is relevant to the likely financial situation and investment objectives of the intended audience of the communication. FINRA stated that, under such reasonably designed policies and procedures, a communication containing projected performance or targeted returns should only be distributed to investors whom a member reasonably believes have access to resources to independently analyze this information and who have the financial expertise to understand the risks and limitations of these types of presentations (referred to herein collectively as ``investors who have the resources and financial expertise'').
